convoLines.text: "So. They'd tell me to keep working. So I'm working. That's the whole plan."
Everett frowns. "Something about the time didn't sit right. Press someone on it — and watch their face."
Said. Now it's theirs to carry.
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"I'm not from Denver. I'm from Columbus, Ohio. I was ashamed of the truth. Out here nobody asks, so I stopped telling."
A long exhale. "I'll get there. Just needed a minute where I didn't have to be fine."
"Have you heard what they're calling Nightlight? Addison is pushing 'Big-Bane'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"And... scene. Good talk."
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Don't mind me. Today's just heavy. Doesn't matter now."
"This one — Pupunha (Peach Palm). Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
Jorge shrugs. "I hear the fire crackle and people talking. That's all I know, and I know it well."
"Most days I don't think about it. Today I am. Appreciate you noticing."
"The whole fire was arguing about Nightlight last night — what to even CALL it. 'Big Big' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"I don't know you well enough for that. Ask me again when we've survived something together."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"About the pantry run — still need hands. Are you in?"
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. Nobody's worked the old burn east of camp in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Lorenzo owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
Everett has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"The fire feels smaller without Lorenzo. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"I hum one note, over and over, when the dark comes for Lorenzo, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.

"We never finished talking about grief — we wandered off it, 3 days back. 'Most days I don't think about it. Today I am. Appreciate you noticing.' We still owe what's been happening a proper ending, too."
Jorge has an edge today — something curdled.
"You're kind. Don't let this place change that."
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "I dreamed Lorenzo was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"About grief — yeah, we never did get back to that."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"I — yeah. It helps, hearing that."
"Nobody says Lorenzo's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
You show them American Hazelnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Alright, duty calls. This was a good pause."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
Back home I was an arborist. Let me show you what that means out here.
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
"Here. I made an extra." Everett presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"Every useful thing I do is a brick. I'm building something with my name on it."
"Back home nobody noticed me. Here — here I could be someone. I need that to be true."
"Still on what they want."
"Right. Sorry, I go on about it. What did you want?"

"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "You want to know what I did in the raid? I stood down Hushpuppy at the treeline — it ran. Don't call it brave. Call it awake."
"I should go before I say something sincere."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"This wound — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"That again?" Aidan sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"No, yeah, of course. Forget I asked." They won't forget. They'll just stop asking.
"Still on that favor."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Okay. I'll manage on my own."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"My therapist would have a field day. If therapists still existed. If days still existed."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
"Here. I made an extra." Everett presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "2 of us are down with a hot angry fever. Boil everything. I mean everything."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching?"
"Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Well. My social battery is officially dead."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
Jorge: "Don't just stand there — you've got opinions, right?"
"This cut — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Could you take a look?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Have you seen the sick row? 2 down with a hot angry fever. Nobody says it out loud but everyone's counting."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"...Actually, forget it."
